Adaptive algorithms

Adaptive DSP equalization for optical links

Compared blind equalizers for polarization-mixed optical signals and developed a variable-momentum CMA path that converged up to eight times faster.

Case study

Make the equalizer respond faster without giving up recovery quality.

CMAVM-CMALMSOptical comms

The problem

Polarization-mode dispersion, phase noise, carrier-frequency offset, and additive noise can rotate and smear received constellations. Standard constant-modulus adaptation is robust but slow; higher-order modulation also complicates its single-radius assumption.

The experiments

I compared standard CMA with momentum, variable-momentum, second-moment, L-BFGS, and multi-modulus variants across SNR, group delay, and filter-tap settings. The strongest improvement came from adapting the momentum term as convergence approached.

Joint correction

A decision-directed LMS formulation was used to estimate equalizer taps and carrier-frequency offset together, keeping the final CFO estimate within five percent of the simulated offset in the tested conditions.

Takeaway

There is no universally best adaptive equalizer: convergence speed, steady-state error, block processing cost, and modulation order all matter. Variable momentum offered a practical improvement because it changed the optimizer’s behavior over the course of adaptation.
